claims.text: No written succession or knowledge-transfer plan for IMERG, PPS or the GSFC labs was found; NASA's OIG reports the agency lacks a workforce planning process, and Goddard's workforce fell over 40 percent from March 2020 to January 2026.
claims.confidence_reason: Oversight reports are direct at agency/center level; IMERG-level absence is by not finding one.
claims.applicability: Agency and center level, not IMERG-specific.

evidence.passage: addressing a retirement wave for the technical | workforce. While these challenges continue this year, | they are exacerbated by workforce reductions occurring | across the Agency. As of July 2025, NASA's workforce | decreased by approximately 20 percent since 2023, | from over 18,000 to roughly 14,000 employees. The | reductions present difficulties to maintaining institutional | knowledge and ensuring the continuity of mission | critical operations. … the OIG, Government Accountability Office, and | National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and | Medicine (National Academies) have all reported on the | Agency's lack of a workforce planning process
evidence.location: p. 12, Sustaining Mission Critical Capabilities (right column, .txt lines 564-583)

evidence.passage: Specifically, from March 2020 to January 2026, Goddard experienced a decrease | of over 40 percent in total workforce. In 2025 alone, Goddard lost approximately a third of its civilian | workforce due to the deferred resignation program.
For many years, Goddard has | grappled with tight annual budgets, a senior workforce increasingly eligible for retirement, aging | infrastructure, and substantial deferred maintenance costs.

When teams experience rapid transitions, there are key steps | that leaders and group members can take to determine | which knowledge gaps must be resolved, provide support for | team members who are learning new roles, and maintain the | team’s knowledge to move forward effectively.

claims.text: PDIR-Now IR estimates for IMERG V07 are computed at PPS from CPC's merged geo-IR, not at UC Irvine; V08 is to use CSU's open GPROF-IR instead, but the Late Run stays on V07 'hybrid' until no sooner than winter 2026.
claims.confidence_reason: ATBD and GPM notices are direct; GPROF-IR's V08 role is from a preprint (abstract checked in the browser); where GPROF-IR will run is not stated.

evidence.passage: Infrared-Rain Rate (PDIR; Nyugen et al. 2020a,b) re-calibration scheme. In parallel, CPC | assembles the zenith-angle-corrected, intercalibrated merged geo-IR fields and forwards them to | PPS for use in the PDIR computation routines.
evidence.location: ATBD V07, page 8, lines 552-555 of txt

evidence.passage: We introduce GPROF-IR, a neural-network-based precipitation retrieval designed to provide precipitation estimates from single-channel geostationary IR observations for the upcoming IMERG V08.

Already, IMERG V07 Late and Early are operating in “hybrid” mode, using the IMERG V07 algorithm but ingesting GPROF V08. … The Late and Early Runs will be in this “hybrid V07” posture until the near-real-time processing system is ready to switch to V08, which is expected to take place no sooner than fall of 2026.

Therefore, at this stage, it seems more likely that IMERG V08 Final Run will be released in the fall of 2026, though this projection assumes that the parent products perform within expected bounds. … The projected switch for the Late and Early Runs will take place no sooner than winter of 2026, with their retrospective records (i.e., beginning 1998) available prior to this switch but after the release of IMERG V08 Final Run.
